chronology.event: Begins funding and organising the UFO disclosure initiative through Rockefeller Family & Associates.
'The Best Available Evidence' briefing document is produced and distributed to officials and legislators worldwide.
GAO publishes its Roswell records report; the report is retained in the Clinton White House Roswell file (2006-0476-F).
President and Mrs Clinton visit Rockefeller's JY Ranch in Jackson, Wyoming - documented in Clinton Library FOIA collection 2006-0546-F.
Initiative winds down without a declassification decision.

conflicts: No declassification order resulted. The White House files that were opened contain public correspondence and the unclassified GAO report rather than any intelligence-community material.

label: Laurance S. Rockefeller
narrative: Rockefeller ran the only serious private attempt to force UFO declassification from inside the American establishment, and he did it with money, access and a written brief rather than a press conference. From 1993 he funded what became known as the Rockefeller Initiative: a coordinated effort to persuade President Clinton to declassify the government's UFO holdings. He financed the compilation of 'Unidentified Flying Objects Briefing Document: The Best Available Evidence,' produced under Marie 'Bootsie' Galbraith with Stanton Friedman and Don Berliner, and distributed it in 1995 to members of Congress, heads of state and senior officials. He raised the subject directly with the Clintons - the Clinton Library's own FOIA collections include a file of correspondence between President Clinton and Laurance Rockefeller (2006-0480-F) and a photographic collection documenting the Clintons' visit to Rockefeller's JY Ranch in Jackson, Wyoming on 21 August 1995 (2006-0546-F), the visit at which he is reported to have pressed the case. The initiative worked through the Office of Science and Technology Policy and the White House science adviser rather than the intelligence community, which is precisely why it failed: OSTP had no jurisdiction over the compartments. What it did produce is a documented record of a private citizen with unmatched access asking a sitting president to open the files, and the president's apparatus declining. The Roswell file the White House did assemble (2006-0476-F) contains the 1995 GAO report and public correspondence - the residue of a request that was routed to the unclassified surface.
